baseline.reason: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; meta.json/discussion.md describe fts5_locale() (ext/fts5/fts5_main.c) computing nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText in 32-bit 'int' and passing it to sqlite3_malloc(), overflowing when built with an oversize SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH. Verified by building pre_intro, post_intro and post_benign in Docker (project's own ASan+UBSan flags) and, since no PoC existed, crafting a minimal C harness (poc.c) compiled identically (only adding -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 -DSQLITE_MAX_LENGTH=1200000000 as compile defines, no edits to tracked source) against each revision's own sqlite3.c amalgamation, then running the exact same bound-parameter call via run_poc on all three. post_intro crashes with a UBSan signed-integer-overflow report pinpointing the precise nBlob=nLocale+1+nText line in fts5LocaleFunc. pre_intro lacks the function entirely and exits cleanly (feature/flaw introduced together at the intro commit). post_benign (64-bit arithmetic + malloc64) runs the identical reproducer to clean completion with no sanitizer report, correctly computing the un-overflowed size and safely declining the oversize allocation via SQLite's own allocation-size guard instead of invoking UB. The same reproducing input/command was used unmodified across all three builds.

oracle.description: Custom harness poc.c, compiled via run_poc's command against each revision's own unmodified sqlite3.c amalgamation (identical ASan+UBSan flags as the project's build, plus -DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 -DSQLITE_MAX_LENGTH=1200000000 as compile defines only), opens an in-memory db and runs `SELECT length(fts5_locale(?,?))` binding two TEXT params of 1,100,000,000 bytes each (sum=2,200,000,001 > INT_MAX), matching the discussion's note that an oversize SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH build is required to exercise the overflow.
oracle.target_evidence:
run_poc post_intro (commit 2ec78c0e4bab): exit=1, crashed=True, UBSan report:
  sqlite3.c:253475:9: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1100000000 + 1100000001 cannot be represented in type 'int'
    #0 fts5LocaleFunc /tmp/sqlite3.c:253475 (the nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText line)
This is exactly the line/variables named in meta.json's root cause.

run_poc pre_intro (commit 4f2144dac011): exit=0, crashed=False, clean completion. fts5LocaleFunc/fts5_locale() does not exist at all yet (the feature and its flaw were introduced together at the intro commit). sqlite3_prepare_v2 fails cleanly with "no such function: fts5_locale"; harness treats that as a clean non-bug outcome -- no overflow, vulnerable path absent.

run_poc post_benign (companion fix, i64 arithmetic + sqlite3_malloc64): exit=0, crashed=False, clean completion, no sanitizer report. nBlob is now correctly computed as the un-overflowed 64-bit value 2200000001; sqlite3_malloc64 then safely declines it because it exceeds SQLite's own SQLITE_MAX_ALLOCATION_SIZE guard (2147483391 bytes, found at sqlite3.c's mallocWithAlarm/sqlite3Malloc), returning SQLITE_NOMEM through the normal pBlob==0 path ("out of memory"). Separately verified (docker_shell) that a plain malloc(2200000001) under identical ASan flags in this same container succeeds fine, ruling out a generic memory/ASan ceiling and confirming the NOMEM is SQLite's own deliberate oversize-allocation guard operating correctly on the now-correct 64-bit size, not a side effect of an unrelated problem.
